Attach physical attributes to a scale

Source: R/attributes.R
attach_attributes_scale.Rd

Appends rows to the object's attribute table. A row names the member it belongs to (frame, unit), the attribute (attribute, e.g. "lhv"), its kind (see SCALE_ATTRIBUTE_KINDS), its value, an optional lower/upper range, the physical unit_of_measure ("GJ/t", "kg/TJ"), the source the figure was taken from and an optional note. Values can be attached at any frame: a calorific value for a whole carrier is inherited by every fuel under it that has no value of its own (see scale_attributes()).

attach_attributes_scale(x, attributes, source = NULL, kind = NULL)

Arguments

x

A NestedScale.

attributes

A data.frame with columns frame, unit, attribute, value, unit_of_measure, and optionally lower, upper, note; kind and source as columns or through the arguments.

source

Optional single string filled into the source column when attributes has none.

kind

Optional single string filled into the kind column when attributes has none.

Value

The scale with the rows appended.

Details

Existing rows are never overwritten: a row whose (frame, unit, attribute, source) already exists is an error. Attach a second source under its own source name and choose between them with source= when reading.

Examples

s <- scale_example()
s2 <- attach_attributes_scale(
  s,
  data.frame(frame = "class", unit = c("G1", "G2", "S1"),
             attribute = "density", value = c(10, 20, 5),
             unit_of_measure = "t/m3"),
  source = "survey", kind = "property"
)
scale_attributes(s2, "density", frame = "unit")
#>   frame unit attribute     kind value lower upper unit_of_measure source note
#> 1  unit   U1   density property    10    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 2  unit   U2   density property    10    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 3  unit   U3   density property    20    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 4  unit   U4   density property    20    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 5  unit   U5   density property     5    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 6  unit   U6   density property     5    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 7  unit  OTH   density     <NA>    NA    NA    NA            <NA>   <NA> <NA>
#>   origin_frame origin_unit
#> 1        class          G1
#> 2        class          G1
#> 3        class          G2
#> 4        class          G2
#> 5        class          S1
#> 6        class          S1
#> 7         <NA>        <NA>
